issue_context.title: Add index name to error message
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**

     "Attribute `id` is not sortable. This index does not have configured sortable attributes.",

**Expected behavior**

I would LOVE to see the name of the index in this message.

     "Attribute `id` is not sortable. index 'Author' does not have configured sortable attributes.",

In particular, I _do_ have sortable attributes:

http://127.0.0.1:7700/indexes/Author/settings

![image](https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/assets/619585/8cb2c9ef-0f13-42c9-8008-a58f938f4e65)

Perhaps the real issue is that the id is the primary key?  More likely I'm using the wrong index, but I can't see what that is.  A link to the settings would be even more awesome!

[EDIT] Indeed, I had something in my code that changed the name of the index, it was getting automatically created but was empty.  Having the index name in the error message would have been very helpful.
comments:
Hello @tacman 
Thank you for this report. 

This would be a nice improvements

Any contribution is welcome ❤️

⚠️ More info for the contributor:

This issue is not hard, but not trivial. Knowledge in Rust are required.
It will probably mean a lot of small mechanical changes to multiple files.

We would probably want the added context for most if not all `milli::UserError` . The thing is that in this location of the engine, we don't have the information of the index name.
So it would have to be injected at the point where the error is caught in the webserver part of the engine, which will be many different points depending on where we're calling milli functions that can error
Perhaps the change could be make in the meilisearch php library?
We would rather handle this at the source (engine) than changing things in 10 library

Makes sense.  In addition to the index, I guess it'd be helpful to have all the details.  Sometimes I run meilisearch in docker, and in different projects it listens on different ports, and sometimes calls a remote server.  So in addition to the index, I'd want to know the server and port.

We would rather not prioritize the port addition to solve this issue -> let's focus on the index name as a first step. From a product perspective, it does not seem relevant to us to have this information in the error, so we need more product discussion before validating it. We are a small team so we are careful about everything we add because can be tedious to update and maintain

Btw, as a workaround, in the meantime you can have all the information in the URL you try to reach: index name and port
I would like to see if I can work on this issue, would that be ok?

Hello @cisco877

For your information, we prefer not assigning people to our issues because sometimes people ask to be assigned and never come back, which discourages the volunteer contributors from opening a PR to fix this issue.

Can someone write me the steps to replicate the issue?
Maybe I can give it a try.

Hey, you should create an index with the method of your choice: https://www.meilisearch.com/docs/reference/api/indexes#create-an-index
For example in terminal you would run:
```
curl \
  -X POST 'http://localhost:7700/indexes' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary '{
    "uid": "movies",
    "primaryKey": "id"
  }'
```

And then do a search with a filter on any field https://www.meilisearch.com/docs/reference/api/search#search-in-an-index-with-post
In terminal again it could be this request:
```
curl \
  -X POST 'http://localhost:7700/indexes/movies/search' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary '{ "filter": "title = Kefirausaurus" }'
```

And this is the response you'll receive:
```json
{
  "message": "Attribute `title` is not filterable. This index does not have configured filterable attributes.\n1:6 title = Kefirausaurus",
  "code":"invalid_search_filter",
  "type":"invalid_request",
  "link":"https://docs.meilisearch.com/errors#invalid_search_filter"
}
```

@irevoire Yes, but I have hundreds of indexes.  "This index" is ambiguous, it'd be trivial to replace that generic term with the index name, so I knew exactly which index was causing the problem.  Especially since you can prefix the indexes when in development, so it's a lot of work to hunt down just the name of the index.
@tacman Yes, I was just giving a reproducer for @postmeback, who wants to work on it
Got it, thanks!

@irevoire Hi, as you said in https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/pull/4414#pullrequestreview-1888056484, we would prefer to added the index name to every milli error message around here: https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/blob/82b43e9a7f09de51ea723817cc0878a77fccf049/index-scheduler/src/error.rs#L118-L119

If I use the manual implementation of From<milli::Error>, do I need to add the index_name to the Error, but then I would not be able to pass the index name to the internal error messages of milli::Error?

Hey @airycanon, thanks for looking into it!

> but then I would not be able to pass the index name to the internal error messages of milli::Erro

I’m not sure I understood this sentence.

I think what you should do is to remove the `From` `milli::Error` implementation of the `index_scheduler::Error` and instead do it by hand.
Also, you should update the error to something like that:
```rust
#[error("Index {index}: {error}")]
Milli { index: String, error: milli::Error }
```

I cannot guarantee you that it’ll be possible everywhere, but _I think_ it should work.
@irevoire Got it. I will give it a try, and thanks for your patience.

@irevoire Hi, after some debugging, I found that adding `index_name` to `index_scheduler::Error` doesn't address the issue described in https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/issues/4392#issuecomment-2270629021. This is because it returns a `MeilisearchHttpError` (defined here: https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/blob/main/meilisearch/src/error.rs#L66).
Do you think I should also add `index_name` to `MeilisearchHttpError`? If so, should I pass the index name to it before it's converted to `ResponseError` in these locations:
* https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/blob/main/meilisearch/src/search/mod.rs#L890
* https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/blob/main/meilisearch/src/search/mod.rs#L768

Hey @airycanon,

Yes, I think you’re right and you should do that!

Hey @airycanon.

> What do you think about this alternative approach?

I can be wrong because I didn’t look at the code like you did, but I feel like this is more error-prone in the sense that we might forget to push the index name in a lot of place since it’s not related to the milli error anymore 🤔 

> I found that I need to modify many functions that return ResponseError to add an index_uid parameter and pass it to MeilisearchHttpError

And about that, aren’t you supposed to modify the exact same number of functions in both case? But in one case you get a compiler error and in the other case you need to find which function you must modify? 
If it’s the case, then I would prefer if we stick to the first approach and make sure we **cannot** forget to specify the index name.
If not, please let me know, I may have overlooked something 🥶
